title: Identification of M-theory's fundamental degrees of freedom and a test of whether it describes nature

concept.text: Strings 2000 problem 7 (proposed by Louise Dolan, Annamaria Sinkovics, and Billy and Linda Rose): what are the fundamental degrees of freedom of M-theory, the theory whose low-energy limit is eleven-dimensional supergravity and which subsumes the five consistent superstring theories, and does the theory describe Nature? Sources given: https://preskill.caltech.edu/millennium.html ; https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v54.i10.14_2.online.pdf ; https://x.com/martinmbauer/status/1779906631003697211.

page.title: Nonperturbative formulation and empirical test of M-theory
page.definition: M-theory’s fundamental quantum variables and dynamics are specified without a weak-coupling expansion, reproducing eleven-dimensional supergravity, its low-energy gravitational field theory, and the five superstring limits. A prediction for a four-dimensional vacuum, a possible ground state, passes an empirical test that distinguishes it from competing descriptions.

goal.need: Five consistent superstring theories describe ten-dimensional limits; M-theory is intended to unite them with an eleven-dimensional quantum description of gravity. Connecting that description to the observed four extended spacetime dimensions requires a specified ground state and calculable observables. The target combines identification of quantum dynamics with an experimental test.

statements.context: Opening passage of problem 7, presented on 15 July 2000. The question also asks whether M-theory describes nature.

statements.quote: Clearly, this is a direction to be pursued.
statements.context: The report discusses string theory, explicitly including M-theory, as an approach to quantum gravity and black-hole information.

statements.body: Gordon Kane, University of Michigan, a developer of string and M-theory phenomenology
statements.quote: What matters is that the predictions of the 10D theory for the 4D world are demonstrably testable and falsifiable.
statements.context: Kane includes eleven-dimensional M-theory in the framework discussed and argues that experiments test specified four-dimensional solutions.

completion.title: A microscopic formulation of M-theory passes a discriminating empirical test.
completion.criterion: A formulation specifies fundamental quantum variables and dynamics and recovers eleven-dimensional supergravity and the five superstring limits. For a specified four-dimensional vacuum, it predicts a numerical observable beyond the data used to choose or fit that vacuum. An independent measurement agrees within the stated theoretical and experimental uncertainties and distinguishes the prediction from specified competing descriptions under the experiment’s published decision criterion. Agreement tests the formulation together with the chosen vacuum.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback, interpreting the two parts of Strings 2000 problem 7.
completion.basis: Strings 2000 problem 7 asks for both microscopic variables and a connection to nature. Searches of that list, National Research Council reports, the BFSS proposal, matrix-theory reviews and string-phenomenology papers found no joint completion criterion or M-theory-wide experimental significance threshold. This fallback combines the two requested outcomes. A successful test of one vacuum would support that model; it would not establish that M-theory is the unique description of nature.

milestones.title: Matrix quantum mechanics reproduces the two-loop v⁶/r¹⁴ graviton interaction from supergravity.
milestones.criterion: Match the coefficient, including normalization, of the v⁶/r¹⁴ interaction between two gravitons, quanta of the gravitational field, in matrix quantum mechanics and eleven-dimensional supergravity, with zero longitudinal momentum transfer. Here v is relative velocity and r is separation; comparison uses the low-velocity, large-separation expansion. Becker and colleagues report agreement at two loops in their paper submitted on 10 June 1997.
milestones.set_by: The matrix-theory scattering consistency test introduced by BFSS and extended to two loops by Becker, Becker, Polchinski and Tseytlin. This test concerns the flat-space matrix-model proposal.
milestones.threshold_quote: Low energy supergravity predicts the coefficient of the $v^6/r^{14}$ term, a two-loop effect, in agreement with explicit matrix model calculation.

milestones.title: The large-N quantum theory has eleven-dimensional Lorentz-invariant scattering amplitudes.
milestones.criterion: Establish eleven-dimensional Lorentz symmetry of quantum scattering as matrix size N tends to infinity, including longitudinal boosts and rotations of the lightlike quantization surface. Tropper and Wang’s paper, published on 19 July 2023, derives the symmetry from a soft-scattering theorem and supplies checks using a string-theory scaling limit. It identifies a derivation directly from the matrix Hamiltonian as further work.
milestones.set_by: BFSS, section 8 of their matrix-model proposal; subsequently investigated by Tropper and Wang. The published criterion was written for the BFSS model.
milestones.threshold_quote: It is clearly important to determine if the matrix model satisfies the angular conditions in the large N limit.

milestones.title: An M-theory compactification yields three chiral families and the Standard Model gauge group.
milestones.criterion: Obtain a four-dimensional effective theory with three families of quarks and leptons coupled to SU(3)C × SU(2)L × U(1)Y, the Standard Model gauge group. Chirality means that left- and right-handed fields transform differently under gauge interactions. Donagi and colleagues construct supersymmetric heterotic M-theory models satisfying this spectrum-level criterion in the preprint submitted on 21 December 1999.
milestones.set_by: The three-family Standard Model spectrum used in particle-physics model building, implemented by Donagi, Ovrut, Pantev and Waldram. Their published construction concerns heterotic M-theory.
milestones.threshold_quote: three families of chiral quarks and leptons coupled to the gauge group $SU(3)_C\times SU(2)_{L}\times U(1)_{Y}$.

milestones.title: A microscopic quantum formulation yields supergravity and all five superstring limits.
milestones.criterion: Specify fundamental quantum variables and dynamics without a weak-coupling expansion, and derive eleven-dimensional supergravity and all five consistent superstring theories in their appropriate limits. The BFSS proposal supplies matrix quantum mechanics for uncompactified flat spacetime. Lin’s review, revised on 18 August 2026, still presents equality of matrix-model and M-theory scattering amplitudes as a conjecture; that proposal alone does not derive all five string limits.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback: searches of Strings 2000 problem 7, the BFSS proposal and matrix-theory reviews found no common acceptance test for a microscopic formulation covering all five string limits.

milestones.title: A four-dimensional M-theory vacuum predicts an experimental signature beyond fitted observations.
milestones.criterion: Derive an experimental signature beyond the observations used to construct a specified four-dimensional vacuum. Cleaver and colleagues state this step after matching existing data. Acharya, Kane and Kumar’s 2012 review discusses a conditional Higgs-boson mass calculation near 125 GeV for a supersymmetric low-energy spectrum; it also acknowledges existing experimental hints near that mass.
milestones.set_by: The string-phenomenology progression articulated by Cleaver and colleagues in their abstract and introduction. Their worked example concerns heterotic strings; Kane and Acharya, Kane and Kumar apply vacuum-based prediction to M-theory.
milestones.threshold_quote: The subsequent goal is to extract potential signatures beyond the observable data.
